_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution. A mutation vocabulary belongs to ONE subset of ONE standard of ONE artifact, so `s.space.home`'s catalog and its no-oracle decision live here rather than in a shared manifest. The launcher artifact is semio-NATIVE and its entire mutable artifact-lane surface is one counter — see `noOracleDecisions` below for why no third party can be authoritative over it.

noOracleDecisions.rationale: `s.space.home` is a semio-NATIVE artifact: its `.shome.dsl.semio` text and `.pack.semio` binary envelopes are written and read by this repository alone, and its whole mutable artifact-lane surface is a single unsigned counter, `catalog_generation`, that no interchange format anywhere models. There is nothing for a third party to be authoritative ABOUT — the counter is a re-materialize trigger bumped after a create/import/delete on the launcher's catalog port, not authored content — so no crate was found, surveyed or declined: the category is empty. Confidence comes instead from the committed specification vector under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/🔢️change-catalog-generation/🧪️tests/bumps-the-catalog-generation-to-7/`, a handcrafted `(before, mutation, after, diff, outcome)` quintet that pins 3 → 7 so an implementation that INCREMENTED rather than SET lands on 4 and fails, and from the inverse law as a metamorphic property: the inverse of a setter can only be built by reading the old value out of BASE, so a leaf that inverted structurally instead cannot restore the document and is caught by `inverse-change-catalog-generation`.
